cards.name: Late dominant side, 25+ bps away
three_sentence_edge: This table exists in the final minute when BTC is already at least 25 bps from the start and the dominant side still asks 70c-98c.
In the current clean sample it appears in 6 markets across 6 days, with 100.0% wins and +11.2% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
The hypothesis is not model alpha; it is buying an almost-settled outcome only when the book has not fully charged for distance from the strike.
cards.execution_note: This is the kind of high-win, low-capacity table to prefer if it survives costs, because it should be easy to explain and hard to scale.

cards.name: Very late dominant side, 50+ bps away
three_sentence_edge: This table exists in the last 30 seconds when BTC is at least 50 bps from the start and the dominant side is not yet priced at a dollar.
In the current clean sample it appears in 1 markets across 1 days, with 100.0% wins and +20.5% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
The hypothesis is a small-capacity cleanup trade: the result is nearly determined but the last resting ask may still be stale or convenience-priced.
cards.execution_note: This should be traded only if live top-of-book capacity is real and cancel/settlement timing is not a source of operational risk.

cards.name: Directional 5s impulse lag
three_sentence_edge: This table exists in the middle of the window after BTC moves at least 5 bps in 5 seconds while the chosen side is still offered between 35c and 80c.
In the current clean sample it appears in 148 markets across 18 days, with 64.2% wins and +5.7% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
The hypothesis is simple repricing lag: external BTC moves first, then thin prediction-market liquidity catches up.
cards.execution_note: Capacity should be tiny and quote life should be short, because stale fills after the impulse reverses are exactly the toxic case.

cards.name: Late near-strike directional control
three_sentence_edge: This table exists late in the window while BTC is still near the strike and the current direction costs 50c-75c.
In the current clean sample it appears in 277 markets across 3 days, with 66.1% wins and +2.1% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
It should be dangerous because tiny BTC noise can flip settlement, so it is included as a near-strike toxicity control.
cards.execution_note: A profitable bot should usually reject this unless live evidence proves the book is structurally mispricing the final minute.

cards.name: Opening near-strike Up, 50c-75c ask
three_sentence_edge: This table exists in the first minute of BTC 5-minute windows when BTC is still within 5 bps of the start and Up is offered between 50c and 75c.
In the current clean sample it appears in 687 markets across 36 days, with 56.0% wins and +3.7% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
The hypothesis is that opening flow overpays for the short-term Down side or is slow to price a tiny Up bias while the market is still anchored near the strike.
cards.execution_note: It is small-capacity: test one entry per market first, with taker economics as the upper bound and maker-minus-1c as a shadow route.

cards.name: Opening near-strike Down, 50c-75c ask
three_sentence_edge: This table is the Down-side mirror of the opening near-strike setup: first minute, BTC within 5 bps, Down ask between 50c and 75c.
In the current clean sample it appears in 728 markets across 37 days, with 50.7% wins and -6.5% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
It tests whether the opening edge is symmetric or whether the current sample is specifically an Up-side table.
cards.execution_note: If the mirror fails, the bot should not generalize the Up rule into a generic near-strike quote engine.

cards.name: Volatile cheap tail up to 5c
three_sentence_edge: This table exists when short-term BTC volatility is elevated and the cheaper side still costs only 2c-5c.
In the current clean sample it appears in 5 markets across 5 days, with 0.0% wins and -100.0% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
The hypothesis is that volatility creates underpriced tails, not that every cheap tail is mispriced.
cards.execution_note: It is a candidate only if it beats the 1c-2c control and has enough repeatable signals to avoid lottery thinking.

cards.name: Cheap tail 1c-2c control
three_sentence_edge: This table exists when the cheaper side is offered at 1c-2c with at least a few seconds left.
In the current clean sample it appears in 679 markets across 39 days, with 0.7% wins and -63.2% $25-per-signal ROI before fees/slippage.
It tests the original small-lottery idea directly: cheap options feel attractive, but they are usually priced cheap for a reason.
cards.execution_note: If this control is negative, do not build a 1c quote engine just because the occasional hit looks good.
